stories.title: Former OpenAI researcher says the Riemann proof matters less than the fact that an AI system can produce it
stories.summary: Complexity theorist Scott Aaronson argues that while AI-generated mathematical breakthroughs might eventually yield scientific applications, the real significance lies in the capability itself. Proving the Riemann hypothesis would not alter daily life, but the fact that an AI can perform such work has staggering implications for humanity.

Mistral Large 4 edges past closed rivals on visual grounding benchmark
stories.summary: Mistral AI claims its new flagship model, Mistral Large 4, outperforms closed frontier models on visual grounding tasks. The company reports a 42% score on the Dense200 benchmark, narrowly beating GPT-6 Astra by one point. An open-weight model leading a closed competitor on vision tasks is notable.

stories.title: Mistral Large 4 visual grounding claim lands at 51st of 73
stories.summary: Mistral claims its Large 4 model outperforms closed frontier models on visual grounding, citing a narrow win over GPT-6 Astra. However, a public vision board ranking 73 models places the system at 51st. The vendor's internal benchmark and the public leaderboard have reached different conclusions.

OpenAI: GPT-6.2 AI helped design proteins that bound to targets
stories.summary: OpenAI reports that its GPT-6.2 model helped design proteins that successfully attached to intended targets in lab tests conducted by partner Onava. While specialist software helped select the candidates, the company suggests the general-purpose model played a role in the design process for these protein candidates.

stories.title: OpenAI Says GPT-6.2 Protein Designs Bound Their Targets in Lab Tests, at a 10.9% Rate - Technology Org
Scientists gave AI a stroke to map its language circuits
stories.summary: Researchers are studying damaged large language models to better understand how neural networks support language processing. By deliberately introducing faults into the systems, scientists aim to map internal circuits in a manner similar to historical studies of human brain injury. The models have developed speech problems.

stories.title: Apple Enters the AI Agent Race as It Takes on OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta. What That Means for AAPL Stock. - Barchart.co
Anthropic's Claude now lets you turn artifacts into apps
stories.summary: Anthropic has updated its Claude platform to allow users to convert interactive artifacts into standalone desktop applications. Previously restricted to the chat interface, these outputs can now be exported as installable software. The company suggests this transition from internal tool to desktop app has various limitations.

stories.title: Anthropic Lets MCP Servers Ship Skills and Run Background Tasks in Claude - TechRepublic
Anthropic expands Claude Code’s review tools with automated fixes and approvals
stories.summary: Anthropic has introduced Claude Ship, a tool designed to handle code reviews, fixes, and approvals for GitHub pull requests. The system automates the resolution of flagged issues based on team-defined rules. It aims to manage the entire workflow from identifying problems to granting final merge permissions.

stories.title: Anthropic Claude Ship: GitHub AI Code Reviews, Fixes, and Approvals - TechRepublic
Anthropic's Claude can now build installable Windows and Mac apps
stories.summary: Anthropic is allowing users to generate and install desktop applications directly from Claude using natural language prompts. The feature, dubbed Install as app, is available across all subscription tiers, including the free plan. Artifacts can now function as standalone software with operating system integration.

stories.title: Claude Ship coding agents: roles and GitHub controls
stories.summary: Anthropic has launched Claude Ship, a workflow tool for GitHub pull requests that combines automated code review with repair and approval functions. While the review component is generally available, the steward and approval features remain in beta. The system automates routine tasks while maintaining team-defined merge permissions.

stories.title: Google Maps is getting Gemini AI in CarPlay
stories.summary: Google is integrating its Gemini AI assistant into Maps for Apple CarPlay users in the United States. The feature allows drivers to ask natural-language, multi-step questions while navigating. The company plans to roll out the conversational assistant to additional countries following the initial domestic release.

stories.title: Google's AI mode can now read your wallet, with Drive coming next
stories.summary: Google is expanding its Personal Intelligence feature to allow AI Mode to access data from Google Wallet, with Google Drive integration expected soon. The company states these connections are strictly opt-in, allowing users to manually enable or disable access to their personal digital information for personalized search answers.

stories.title: Google's Gemini lands on Android Auto
stories.summary: Gemini has replaced the traditional Google Assistant as the primary voice interface for Android Auto. The update introduces a sparkle icon to the car display and enables more conversational question-handling for navigation, messaging, and trip planning. The system is now the core gateway for in-car voice interaction.

stories.title: IndiaAI Mission launches Chariot-1 foundation models
stories.summary: Chariot Artificial Intelligence has launched its Chariot-1 suite, featuring a large language model and text-to-speech system developed under the IndiaAI Mission. The startup is among the first four teams selected to build sovereign foundation models. The models are designed to address India's linguistic and computational requirements.

stories.title: Karnataka announces AI skilling programme for 63,200 learners
stories.summary: Karnataka has signed agreements with Google, Salesforce, Pega Systems, Sarvam AI and Gnani.ai to provide AI training to 63,200 students and professionals. The state government announced the initiative at the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026. The programme aims to reach engineering and diploma students across the state.

stories.title: Every raises $17.5 million Series A
stories.summary: Media and software company Every has raised a $17.5 million Series A round at a $110 million valuation. Led by IA Ventures, the funding follows a $2 million seed round last year. The company operates a subscription service for individuals and teams navigating the age of AI.

stories.title: XEBO.ai raises $10.5 million for customer experience platform
stories.summary: Dubai-based XEBO.ai has raised $10.5 million in its first institutional funding round from Emirates Growth Fund. The company plans to use the capital to expand its AI-powered experience management platform into North America. It has set a long-term target of reaching $100 million in annual recurring revenue.

stories.title: Mawj raises Series A to automate customer service
stories.summary: Riyadh-based Mawj has raised a Series A round led by SEEDRA Ventures to expand its AI agents that handle customer calls in Saudi and Gulf dialects. The startup claims over 70 percent of inquiries are resolved without human involvement. The size of the investment remains undisclosed.

stories.title: Vegapay raises $10 million Series A
stories.summary: Fintech infrastructure startup Vegapay has raised $10 million in a Series A round co-led by Vertex Ventures and Prosus. The company plans to use the funds to expand its credit infrastructure for banks and financial institutions. Existing investors Elevation Capital and Eximius Ventures also participated in the round.

stories.title: Former xAI employees launch forecasting startup Epochal
stories.summary: Former xAI employees have founded Epochal to develop AI technology for predicting future events. The company's first product, Time Portal, allows AI agents to reconstruct the state of the internet on specific past dates using archived data. The startup aims to assist with forecasting future outcomes.

Google researchers use Gemini 4 to prove 70-year-old math conjecture
stories.summary: Researchers from Google and the University of Illinois have used an experimental system built on the Gemini 4 model to prove Hadwiger’s covering conjecture. The six-page proof was verified by the Lean computer proof assistant. The conjecture had remained unsolved since 1957. Geometry is now being automated.

stories.title: Clifford Chance advises G42 and Inception42 on OpenAI partnership
stories.summary: Clifford Chance has advised G42 and Inception42 on a five-year strategic partnership with OpenAI. The collaboration aims to accelerate AI adoption across the UAE by integrating frontier models into government, business, and educational institutions. The partnership intends to bring technology closer to the organisations shaping how the region learns.

stories.title: Scott Aaronson suggests AI labs may have cryptography breakthroughs
stories.summary: Computer scientist Scott Aaronson says he is virtually certain that OpenAI or Anthropic possess cryptography breakthroughs that could threaten RSA encryption. He cites reports of a potential polynomial-time algorithm for factoring large numbers. The rumors have spread across the tech industry as labs continue their research.

stories.title: AI factoring rumors and the state of RSA encryption
stories.summary: Quantum computing researcher Scott Aaronson has shared reports that OpenAI or Anthropic may have discovered a method for factoring large numbers. If true, the breakthrough would threaten RSA encryption. Bitcoin remains unaffected as it relies on elliptic curve signatures rather than RSA. The threat is currently theoretical.

stories.summary: AI labs rumored to have breakthrough in RSA vulnerability. stories.title: OpenAI model identifies author of 200-year-old sketchbook
stories.summary: OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra model identified the author of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook in 22 minutes. The task had previously stumped professional historians. The finding, disclosed by a history professor, suggests that AI reasoning can extend into non-deterministic disciplines. History is now being processed by models.

stories.title: Noam Brown says current AI models cannot build a poker bot
stories.summary: OpenAI research scientist Noam Brown says that even the most advanced AI models cannot yet build a competitive poker bot on their own. Brown, who previously developed poker-playing software, suggests this limitation highlights areas where human judgment remains necessary. The models are still learning the game.

stories.title: Anthropic agents formalize Fermat's Last Theorem
stories.summary: Anthropic researcher Lance Martin reported that 1,000 Claude agents formalized Andrew Wiles' proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours. The agents autonomously created database tables to manage roles and verify Lean code. The lead agent began organizing the project without being told to do so.

stories.summary: Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners including Dell and Super Micro to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. The move follows new U.S. export controls aimed at preventing Chinese companies from accessing advanced chips through remote data centers in the region. The pause is indefinite.

stories.title: AI-linked job cuts double among European employers
stories.summary: More than one in four European employers report job cuts linked to AI, up from 13% last year. Research from Littler’s 2026 European Employer Survey also shows that 32% of companies have reduced hiring due to AI. The technology is no longer considered just a future concern.

stories.title: AI to transform 38 million Indian jobs by 2030
stories.summary: EY estimates that generative AI could transform 38 million jobs in India by 2030, while Bain and Company projects a talent shortfall of one million people by 2027. Enrolments in specialised AI courses have surged, with security-focused training rising 296% year-on-year as professionals attempt to keep pace.

Australia passes Digital Duty of Care Act
stories.summary: Australia’s new law requires tech companies to identify and reduce risks to users before harm occurs. Platforms, including AI chatbots and social media, face fines of up to 5% of global turnover for non-compliance. Companies are explicitly prohibited from citing the cost of safety as a reason to act.

stories.title: IFF criticises TRAI draft for lack of user recourse
stories.summary: The Internet Freedom Foundation says the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India's draft guidelines on AI provide no way for users to contest automated decisions. The group has requested an extension to the November 27 comment deadline to allow for a more thorough review of the proposed framework.

stories.title: OpenAI faces California lawsuit over safety failures
stories.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging the company failed to ensure the safety of its AI models. The action coincides with scrutiny from federal lawmakers regarding the Department of Justice's involvement in a copyright dispute involving the firm's training data.

research.title: A Hierarchy of Risk Certificates for Representation-Based Prediction
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Representation-based prediction underlies many machine-learning systems. Yet a fitted predictor's failure to meet an accuracy requirement does not establish that its representation-decoder class cannot meet it. We study optimal population mean squared error (MSE) over Lipschitz. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: AI-human hybrid conversations: Can AI Agents Improve Discourse Quality?
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Conversations are central to how people exchange information, share experiences, and develop collective understanding. Yet, across conversational settings, discussions often suffer from uneven participation, unanswered contributions, and a narrow range of perspectives. As generative AI agents. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Attributing Agentic Failure in Reasoning Vision-Language Models with Interactive 2D Environments
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic benchmarks report a success rate that confounds distinct causes of failure: misreading the environment, never working out how components of the environment operates, operating the components in the wrong order, and failing to recover from. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Change Partners at Every Layer: Balanced Random Regrouping for Model Merging
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Model merging combines fine-tuned experts into one model that serves many tasks without retraining, but merging many experts this way substantially reduces accuracy. Grouping offers a middle ground: at every layer or weight matrix, the $N$. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Code availability is not enough: schemas for documenting and extending data analysis
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: A data analysis involves a sequence of decisions, from data cleaning to model specification, each of which can affect the reported result. Reproducing that result is not the same as understanding the sequence of decisions that. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Context Scaling: A New Frontier of AI Scaling
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Many failures of deployed AI arise not from weak inference but from a mismatch between the state a task depends on and the context available when the system acts. Relevant user state, repository revisions, tool traces. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Controllable CAD Generation and Interactive Editing of Fluid Rotors
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Computer-aided design (CAD) provides the geometric foundation for rotors in fluid rotating machinery. However, creating models for different rotors requires different modeling processes, making it difficult to control geometry through design intent and reuse existing models. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Deep Learning-Based Mesoscopic Emission Modeling
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Traffic-related emissions are a major contributor to urban air pollution. However, existing emission models face a fundamental trade-off: macroscopic models are computationally efficient but rely on average speeds, leading to systematic errors, while microscopic models achieve. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
